units.zh: 《易》曰：定天下之吉兇，成天下之亹亹，莫善於蓍龜。
units.en: The Book of Changes says: To discern fortune and ruin for the realm and to sustain its ceaseless work, nothing surpasses divination by milfoil and tortoise.
units.literal: The Book of Changes says: To settle the auspice and bane of the realm and to accomplish the realm’s tireless striving, nothing is better than milfoil and tortoise.

units.zh: 是故天生神物，聖人則之。
units.en: Heaven produces sacred things, and the sage models himself upon them.
units.literal: Therefore Heaven produces numinous things, and the sage takes them as his model.

units.zh: 又神農、桐君論《本草》藥性，黃帝、岐伯說病候治方，皆聖人之所重也。
units.en: Shennong and Lord Tong classified herbs in the Root Canon; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo set forth disease and cure—all arts the sages held dear.
units.literal: Again, Shennong and Lord Tong discussed the properties of drugs in the Root Canon of Materia Medica; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo explained symptoms and healing prescriptions—all were prized by sages.

units.zh: 故太史公著《龜策》、《日者》及《扁鵲倉公傳》，皆所以廣其聞見，昭示後昆。
units.en: Hence Sima Qian’s treatises on tortoise divination, day-selection, and the physicians Bian Que and Lord Cang—all to widen what we know and guide posterity.
units.literal: Thus Grand Historian Sima Qian wrote the “Treatises on Tortoises and Divination,” “The Day Diviners,” and the “Biographies of Bian Que and Lord Cang”—all to broaden knowledge and show the way to later generations.

units.zh: 齊氏作霸以來，招引英俊，但有藝能，無不畢策，今並錄之以備《方伎》云。
units.en: Since Qi began its rise, it has gathered talent; anyone with a craft was pressed into service. They are recorded here for the account of Arts and Techniques.
units.literal: Since Qi rose to hegemony, it has recruited outstanding men; whoever had any skill was exhaustively enlisted. Now all are recorded here to complete the “Arts and Techniques.”

units.zh: 由吾道榮，琅邪人。
units.en: Youwu Daorong was from Langye.
units.literal: Youwu Daorong was a native of Langye.

units.zh: 少好道法，與其同類相求，入長白、太山潛隱，具聞道術。
units.en: As a youth he loved Daoist practice; with kindred spirits he withdrew to Mount Changbai and Mount Tai and mastered the arts of the Way.
units.literal: In youth he loved the Way and its methods; with like-minded companions he sought one another, entered Mount Changbai and Mount Tai to live in seclusion, and heard the full range of Daoist arts.

units.zh: 仍遊鄒、魯之間，習儒業。
units.en: He later wandered between Zou and Lu and studied the classics.
units.literal: He then traveled between Zou and Lu and studied Confucian learning.

units.zh: 晉陽人某，大明法術，乃尋之。
units.en: A man of Jinyang, deeply versed in the arts, set out to find him.
units.literal: A certain man of Jinyang, greatly skilled in the arts, therefore went in search of him.

units.zh: 是人為人家庸力，無識之者，久乃訪知。
units.en: The man was a hired hand in a private home; none knew his worth until a long search revealed him.
units.literal: This man was hired labor in someone’s household; no one knew who he was, and only after a long search was he found out.

units.zh: 其人道家符水、咒禁、陰陽歷數、天文、藥性無不通解，以道榮好尚，乃悉授之。
units.en: He knew talismans, spells, calendrics, astronomy, and medicine; seeing Dao Rong’s devotion, he taught him all of it.
units.literal: The man was thoroughly versed in Daoist talismanic water, incantatory prohibitions, yin-yang calendrics, astronomy, and pharmacology; because Dao Rong admired these things, he taught him everything.

units.zh: 是人謂道榮雲：「我本恒岳仙人，有少罪過，為天官所謫。
units.en: The man told Dao Rong, “I am an immortal of Mount Heng, banished for a minor fault by heaven’s officers.
units.literal: The man said to Dao Rong, “I am originally an immortal of Mount Heng; for a small offense I was demoted by the celestial offices.

units.zh: 今限滿將歸，卿宜送吾至汾水。」
units.en: My term is up and I must return—escort me to the Fen.”
units.literal: My term is now ending and I am about to return; you should escort me to the Fen River.”

units.zh: 及河，值水暴長，橋壞，船渡艱難。
units.en: At the river the flood had burst its banks, the bridge was gone, and boats could scarcely cross.
units.literal: When they reached the river, the water had swollen violently, the bridge was broken, and crossing by boat was difficult.

units.zh: 是人乃臨水禹步，以一符投水中，流便絕。
units.en: He paced the Yu steps at the bank and threw a talisman into the water; the current halted.
units.literal: The man then performed Yu’s paces beside the water and cast a talisman into the stream; the current stopped at once.

units.zh: 俄頃水積將至天，是人徐自沙石上渡。
units.en: Water piled to the sky; he walked calmly across on the stones of the ford.
units.literal: In a moment the piled water rose nearly to the sky; the man slowly crossed over on the sand and stones.

units.zh: 唯道榮見其如是，傍人咸云水如此長，此人遂能浮過，共驚異之。
units.en: Only Dao Rong saw how it was done; onlookers, seeing him cross such a flood, were astounded.
units.literal: Only Dao Rong saw him do this; bystanders all said that with water so high this man could still float across, and together they marveled.

units.zh: 道榮仍歸本部，隱於琅邪山，辟穀，餌松術、茯苓，求長生之秘。
units.en: Dao Rong went home to Mount Langye, lived on pine and tuckahoe, abstained from grain, and sought immortality.
units.literal: Dao Rong returned to his home region, hid on Mount Langye, abstained from grain, ate pine shoots and tuckahoe, and sought the secret of long life.

units.zh: 尋為顯祖追往晉陽。
units.en: Soon Xianzu summoned him to Jinyang.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned by Emperor Xianzu to Jinyang.

units.zh: 至遼陽山中，有猛獸去馬十步，所追人驚怖將走。
units.en: In the Liaoyang hills a beast blocked the road ten paces from the horses; the escort panicked and nearly fled.
units.literal: In the mountains of Liaoyang a fierce beast stood ten paces from the horses; those in pursuit were terrified and about to flee.

units.zh: 道榮以杖畫地成火坑，猛獸遽走。
units.en: Dao Rong traced a fiery pit with his staff, and the beast bolted.
units.literal: Dao Rong drew a fire pit on the ground with his staff, and the beast fled at once.

units.zh: 俄值國廢，道榮歸周。
units.en: When Qi fell, Dao Rong entered Zhou service.
units.literal: Soon the state was abolished, and Dao Rong went over to Zhou.

units.zh: 隋初乃卒。
units.en: He died in early Sui times.
units.literal: In the early Sui he died.

units.zh: 又有張遠遊者，顯祖時令與諸術士合九轉金丹。
units.en: Zhang Yuanyou, in Xianzu’s day, was set to refine the ninefold golden elixir with other adepts.
units.literal: There was also Zhang Yuanyou; in Xianzu’s time he was ordered to compound the nine-times-transmuted golden elixir with other masters of the arts.

units.zh: 及成，顯祖置之玉匣，云：「我貪世間作樂，不能卽飛上天，待臨死時取服。」
units.en: When the elixir was ready, Xianzu locked it in a jade box: “I love the world too well to ascend now—I will swallow it on my deathbed.”
units.literal: When it was finished, Xianzu placed it in a jade casket and said, “I am greedy for the pleasures of the world and cannot at once fly up to Heaven; I shall take it when I am about to die.”

units.zh: 王春，河東人，少好易占，明風角，遊於趙、魏之間，飛符上天。
units.en: Wang Chun of Hedong loved the Changes in youth, read the winds, wandered Zhao and Wei, and was famed for sending talismans heavenward.
units.literal: Wang Chun was a native of Hedong; in youth he loved Changes divination, understood wind angles, traveled between Zhao and Wei, and sent talismans flying to Heaven.

units.zh: 高祖起於信都，引為館客。
units.en: When Gaozu raised his banner at Xindu, Chun became his house diviner.
units.literal: When Gaozu rose at Xindu, Chun was brought in as a house guest.

units.zh: 韓陵之戰，四面受敵，從寅至午，三合三離。
units.en: At Hanling they were surrounded; from dawn to noon they clashed three times and broke off three times.
units.literal: At the battle of Hanling they were attacked on all sides; from the yin hour to the wu hour they joined battle three times and broke off three times.

units.zh: 高祖將退軍，春叩馬諫曰：「比未時，必當大捷。」
units.en: Gaozu meant to retreat; Chun caught his bridle: “Before mid-afternoon you will win decisively.”
units.literal: Gaozu was about to withdraw; Chun seized his horse’s bridle and remonstrated, “By the wei hour there will certainly be a great victory.”

units.zh: 遽縛其子詣王為質，不勝請斬之。
units.en: He bound his son and offered him as a hostage, asking that the son be beheaded if his prediction proved wrong.
units.literal: He immediately bound his son and brought him to the prince as a hostage, begging that if he was wrong his son be beheaded.

units.zh: 俄而賊大敗。
units.en: Soon the enemy was routed.
units.literal: Before long the enemy was utterly defeated.

units.zh: 其後每從征討，其言多中，位徐州刺史，卒。
units.en: On later campaigns his forecasts usually proved right; he became inspector of Xu Province and died in office.
units.literal: Thereafter on every campaign his words mostly hit true; he rose to Inspector of Xu Province and died.

units.zh: 信都芳，河間人。
units.en: Xindu Fang was from Hejian.
units.literal: Xindu Fang was a native of Hejian.

units.zh: 少明算術，為州裏所稱。
units.en: From youth he excelled at mathematics and was praised locally.
units.literal: In youth he was skilled in calculation and was praised in his district.

units.zh: 有巧思，每精研究，忘寢與食，或墜坑坎。
units.en: Ingenious and obsessive, he forgot food and sleep over his work and once fell into a ditch.
units.literal: He had ingenious thought; whenever he studied closely he forgot sleep and food and sometimes fell into pits and ditches.

units.zh: 嘗語人云：「算之妙，機巧精微，我每一沈思，不聞雷霆之聲也。」
units.en: He said, “Calculation is so subtle that when I ponder it I hear no thunder.”
units.literal: He once told someone, “The subtlety of calculation—its ingenuity and fineness—whenever I ponder deeply I do not hear the sound of thunder.”

units.zh: 其用心如此。
units.en: Such was his concentration.
units.literal: Such was the concentration of his mind.

units.zh: 以術數干高祖為館客，授參軍丞相倉曹。
units.en: He offered his arts to Gaozu, became a house guest, and was made staff officer in the chancellor’s granary bureau.
units.literal: By numerology he sought Gaozu and became a house guest, appointed Staff Officer in the Chancellor’s Granary Bureau.

units.zh: 祖珽謂芳曰：「律管吹灰，術甚微妙，絕來旣久，吾思所不至，卿試思之。」
units.en: Zu Ting said, “The pitch-pipe ash test is subtle and long lost—I cannot recover it; try.”
units.literal: Zu Ting said to Fang, “Blowing ash through pitch-pipes is an extremely subtle art long lost; I cannot think it through—try to work it out.”

units.zh: 芳遂留意，十數日，便云：「吾得矣，然終須河內葭莩灰。」
units.en: Fang labored ten days and said, “I have it—but only with reed-ash from Henei.”
units.literal: Fang then applied himself; in a dozen days he said, “I have it—but in the end we need reed-ash from Henei.”

units.zh: 後得河內葭莩，用其術，應節便飛，餘灰卽不動也。
units.en: With Henei reed-ash the ash leapt at each season’s turn; other ash stayed still.
units.literal: Later they obtained Henei reed-ash; using his method, at the proper season it flew, while other ashes did not move.

units.zh: 不為時所重，竟不行，故此法遂絕云。
units.en: The court ignored him, the method was never used, and the art died out.
units.literal: He was not valued by his time and the method was never put into practice, so the art died out.

units.zh: 芳又撰次古來渾天、地動、欹器、漏刻諸巧事，並畫圖，名曰《器準》。
units.en: He compiled ancient devices—armillary spheres, seismoscopes, tipping vessels, clepsydras—illustrated them in Standards of Instruments.
units.literal: Fang also compiled ancient ingenious devices—the armillary sphere, earthquake indicator, tipping vessel, and clepsydra—illustrated them, and titled the work Standards of Instruments.

units.zh: 又著《樂書》、《遁甲經》、《四術周髀宗》。
units.en: He also wrote Books of Music, the Classic of Hidden Stem, and Four Arts and the Gnomon of the Zhou.
units.literal: He also wrote Books of Music, the Classic of Hidden Stem, and the Four Arts and Gnomon of the Zhou Tradition.

units.zh: 芳又私撰歷書，名為《靈憲歷》，算月有頻大頻小，食必以朔，證據甚甄明，每云：「何承天亦為此法，不能精，靈憲若成，必當百代無異議。」
units.en: His private Spiritual Constitution Calendar tracked the moon’s varying size and fixed eclipses at new moon with rare clarity. “He Chengtian tried this but lacked precision,” he said; “finish this calendar and posterity will not quarrel.”
units.literal: Fang also privately drafted a calendar called the Spiritual Constitution Calendar, calculating that the moon is sometimes large and sometimes small and that eclipses must fall on new moon; the evidence was very clear. He often said, “He Chengtian also used this method but could not refine it; if the Spiritual Constitution is completed, for a hundred generations there will be no dispute.”

units.zh: 書未就而卒。
units.en: He died before the book was finished.
units.literal: The book was unfinished when he died.

units.zh: 宋景業，廣宗人。
units.en: Song Jingye was from Guangzong.
units.literal: Song Jingye was a native of Guangzong.

units.zh: 明《周易》，為陰陽，緯候之學，兼明歷數。
units.en: He mastered the Changes, yin-yang lore, weft-text prophecy, and calendrics.
units.literal: He understood the Book of Changes, practiced yin-yang and weft-text prognostication, and was also skilled in calendrics.

units.zh: 魏末，任北平守。
units.en: At the end of Wei he governed Beiping.
units.literal: At the end of Wei he served as Administrator of Beiping.

units.zh: 顯祖作相，在晉陽，景業因高德政上言：「《易稽覽圖》曰：『《鼎》，五月，聖人君，天與延年齒，東北水中，庶人王，高得之。』
units.en: While Xianzu was chief minister at Jinyang, Jingye reported through Gao Dezheng: “The Appraisal Diagram of the Changes reads: ‘Ding, the fifth month—a sage reigns; Heaven grants long life; in the northeastern waters a commoner becomes king; Gao shall obtain it.’
units.literal: When Xianzu was chief minister at Jinyang, Jingye through Gao Dezheng submitted: “The Changes Appraisal Diagram says: ‘The Hexagram Ding, in the fifth month—a sage rules; Heaven grants extended years; in the northeastern waters a common man becomes king; Gao obtains it.’

units.zh: 謹案東北水謂渤海也，高得之，明高氏得天下也。」
units.en: The northeastern waters are Bohai; ‘Gao obtains it’ means the Gao will take the realm.”
units.literal: Examining the text, the northeastern waters mean Bohai; Gao obtains it—this shows the Gao clan will gain the realm.”

units.zh: 是時魏武定八年五月也。
units.en: This was the fifth month of Wei Wuding year eight.
units.literal: It was then the fifth month of the eighth year of Wuding in Wei.

units.zh: 高德政、徐之才並勸顯祖應天受禪，乃之鄴。
units.en: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai urged Xianzu to take the throne, and he marched on Ye.
units.literal: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai both urged Xianzu to accept Heaven’s mandate; he then went to Ye.

units.zh: 至平城都，諸大臣沮計，將還。
units.en: At Pingcheng the ministers dissuaded him and he nearly turned back.
units.literal: When he reached Pingcheng capital, the great ministers discouraged the plan and he was about to return.

units.zh: 賀拔仁等又云：「景業誤王，宜斬之以謝天下。」
units.en: Heba Ren urged, “Jingye misled you—behead him to satisfy the realm.”
units.literal: Heba Ren and others also said, “Jingye has misled the prince; he should be beheaded to appease the realm.”

units.zh: 顯祖曰：「景業當為帝王師，何可殺也。」
units.en: Xianzu said, “Jingye is fit to teach emperors—he cannot be killed.”
units.literal: Xianzu said, “Jingye will be the emperor’s teacher—how can he be killed?”

units.zh: 還至幷，顯祖令景業筮，遇《乾》之《鼎》。
units.en: Back at Bing, Xianzu had Jingye cast the hexagrams and drew Qian changing to Ding.
units.literal: Returning to Bing, Xianzu ordered Jingye to divine and obtained Qian changing to Ding.

units.zh: 景業曰：「《乾》為君，天也。
units.en: Jingye said, “Qian is the ruler—it is Heaven.
units.literal: Jingye said, “Qian is the ruler—Heaven.

units.zh: 《易》曰：『時乘六龍以禦天。』
units.en: The Changes says, “He rides six dragons to govern Heaven.”
units.literal: The Changes says: “In season he rides the six dragons to govern Heaven.”

units.zh: 《鼎》，五月卦也。
units.en: Ding is the fifth-month hexagram.
units.literal: Ding is the hexagram of the fifth month.

units.zh: 宜以仲夏吉辰御天受禪。」
units.en: Take the throne on an auspicious midsummer day.”
units.literal: You should on an auspicious day in midsummer mount Heaven and receive the abdication.”

units.zh: 或曰：「陰陽書，五月不可入官，犯之卒於其位。」
units.en: Others cited yin-yang taboos: “The fifth month forbids taking office—violators die in their posts.”
units.literal: Someone said, “In books of yin-yang, the fifth month is forbidden for entering office; to violate it is to die in one’s post.”

units.zh: 景業曰：「此乃大吉，王為天子，無復下期，豈得不終於其位。」
units.en: Jingye answered, “That is excellent: as Son of Heaven you have no term to end—how would you not die in office?”
units.literal: Jingye said, “This is in fact great good fortune: when the prince becomes Son of Heaven there is no next term—how could he not end in his post?”

units.zh: 顯祖大悅。
units.en: Xianzu was delighted.
units.literal: Xianzu was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 天保初，授散騎侍郎。
units.en: At the opening of Tianbao he was made gentleman attendant at the palace secretariat.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 又有荊次德，有術數，預知尒朱榮成敗，又言代魏者齊。
units.en: Jing Cide, versed in numerology, foretold Erzhu Rong’s fall and declared that Qi would replace Wei.
units.literal: There was also Jing Cide, skilled in numerology, who foretold the success or failure of Erzhu Rong and also said that Qi would replace Wei.

units.zh: 葛榮聞之，故自號齊王。
units.en: Ge Rong heard this and took the title King of Qi.
units.literal: When Ge Rong heard this, he therefore styled himself King of Qi.

units.zh: 待次德以殊禮，問其天人之事。
units.en: Ge Rong honored him and asked about heaven and earth.
units.literal: He treated Cide with exceptional courtesy and asked him about affairs of Heaven and man.

units.zh: 對曰：「齊當興，東海出天子，今王據渤海，是齊地。
units.en: Cide answered, “Qi will rise; a Son of Heaven will come from the Eastern Sea. You hold Bohai—that is Qi’s ground.
units.literal: He replied, “Qi is about to rise; a Son of Heaven will come from the Eastern Sea. Your Majesty now holds Bohai—that is Qi territory.

units.zh: 又太白與月幷，宜速用兵，遲則不吉。」
units.en: Venus stands with the moon—strike at once; delay is ill-omened.”
units.literal: Moreover Venus and the moon are together; you should use troops quickly—delay is unlucky.”

units.zh: 榮不從也。
units.en: Rong ignored him.
units.literal: Rong did not follow this.

units.zh: 許遵，高陽人。
units.en: Xu Zun was from Gaoyang.
units.literal: Xu Zun was a native of Gaoyang.

units.zh: 明《易》，善筮，兼曉天文、風角、占相、逆刺，其驗若神。
units.en: He mastered the Changes and milfoil, astronomy, wind lore, physiognomy, and geomantic needles—with uncanny accuracy.
units.literal: He understood the Changes, was skilled at milfoil divination, and also knew astronomy, wind angles, physiognomy, and reverse needle techniques; his verification was like a spirit’s.

units.zh: 高祖引為館客，自言祿命不富貴，不橫死，是以任性疏誕，多所犯忤，高祖常容惜之。
units.en: Gaozu kept him as house diviner; Zun said his fate held neither riches nor violent death, so he spoke freely and often gave offense, yet Gaozu indulged him.
units.literal: Gaozu brought him in as a house guest; Zun said himself that his allotted fate was not wealth and nobility and that he would not die a violent death, and therefore he was willful, unrestrained, and often offensive, yet Gaozu always indulged him.

units.zh: 邙陰之役，遵謂李業興曰：「彼為火陣，我木陣，火勝木，我必敗。」
units.en: At the Mang’s north bank he told Li Yexing, “Their formation is fire, ours wood—fire defeats wood; we will lose.”
units.literal: In the campaign on the north bank of the Mang, Zun said to Li Yexing, “They have a fire formation and we a wood formation; fire overcomes wood—we are certain to lose.”

units.zh: 果如其言。
units.en: It happened as he said.
units.literal: It turned out exactly as he said.

units.zh: 清河王岳以遵為開府田曹記室。
units.en: Prince Qinghe Yue made him recorder in his field bureau.
units.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yue appointed Zun recorder in the opening staff’s field bureau.

units.zh: 岳封王，以告遵，遵曰：「蜜蜂亦作王。」
units.en: When Yue became a prince, Zun remarked, “Bees make kings too.”
units.literal: When Yue was enfeoffed prince, he told Zun; Zun said, “Bees also make kings.”

units.zh: 岳後將救江陵，遵曰：「此行必致後凶，宜辭疾勿去。」
units.en: When Yue prepared to relieve Jiangling, Zun warned, “This march brings disaster—plead illness and stay.”
units.literal: Later, when Yue was about to march to relieve Jiangling, Zun said, “This expedition will bring later calamity; you should plead illness and not go.”

units.zh: 岳曰：「勢不免去，正當與君同行。」
units.en: Yue said, “I cannot refuse—I ought to take you along.”
units.literal: Yue said, “I cannot avoid going; I should go with you.”

units.zh: 遵曰：「好與生人相隨，不欲共死人同路。」
units.en: Zun said, “I keep company with the living—I will not share a road with the dead.”
units.literal: Zun said, “I like to keep company with the living and do not wish to travel the same road as the dead.”

units.zh: 還。
units.en: He stayed behind.
units.literal: He returned.

units.zh: 岳至京尋喪。
units.en: Yue reached the capital and soon died.
units.literal: Yue reached the capital and soon died.

units.zh: 顯祖無道日甚，遵語人曰：「多折算來，吾筮此狂夫何時當死。」
units.en: As Xianzu grew more lawless, Zun said, “I keep casting when this madman will die.”
units.literal: As Xianzu’s lawlessness grew daily, Zun told people, “I have calculated repeatedly when this madman will die.”

units.zh: 遂布算滿床，大言曰：「不出冬初，我乃不見。」
units.en: He spread rods across his bed and cried, “Before winter I shall not see him.”
units.literal: He spread counting-rods over the bed and declared loudly, “Before the beginning of winter I shall not see him.”

units.zh: 顯祖以十月崩，遵果以九月死。
units.en: Xianzu died in the tenth month; Zun died in the ninth as he foretold.
units.literal: Xianzu died in the tenth month; Zun indeed died in the ninth.

units.zh: 吳遵世，字季緒，渤海人，少學《易》，入恒山從隱居道士遊處。
units.en: Wu Zunshi, styled Jixu, was from Bohai; he studied the Changes in youth and lived with a hermit priest on Mount Heng.
units.literal: Wu Zunshi, courtesy name Jixu, was a native of Bohai; in youth he studied the Changes and entered Mount Heng to wander with a reclusive Daoist priest.

units.zh: 數年，忽見一老翁謂之云：「授君開心符。」
units.en: After years an old man said, “I give you the Heart-Opening Talisman.”
units.literal: After several years an old man suddenly said to him, “I give you the talisman that opens the heart.”

units.zh: 遵世跪取吞之，遂明占候。
units.en: Zunshi knelt, swallowed it, and became a master of divination.
units.literal: Zunshi knelt, took it, and swallowed it; thereafter he was clear in prognostication.

units.zh: 後出遊京洛，以《易》筮知名。
units.en: In the capital he became famed for the Changes.
units.literal: Later he traveled to the capital region and became famous for Changes divination.

units.zh: 魏武帝之將卽位也，使遵世筮之，遇《明夷》之《賁》曰：「初登于天，後入于地。」
units.en: Before Wei Wudi took the throne, Zunshi cast Mingyi changing to Bi: “First he rises to heaven, then he goes into the earth.”
units.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was about to ascend the throne, he had Zunshi divine and obtained Mingyi changing to Bi, saying, “First he ascends to Heaven, afterward he enters the earth.”

units.zh: 帝曰：「何謂也？」
units.en: The emperor asked, “What does that mean?”
units.literal: The emperor said, “What does that mean?”

units.zh: 遵世曰：「初登于天，當作天子。
units.en: Zunshi said, “Rising to heaven means he becomes Son of Heaven.
units.literal: Zunshi said, “First ascending to Heaven—he will become Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 後入于地，不得久也。」
units.en: Entering the earth means his reign will not last.”
units.literal: Entering the earth afterward—he will not long remain.”

units.zh: 終如其言。
units.en: It ended exactly as he said.
units.literal: In the end it was as he said.

units.zh: 世祖以丞相在京師居守，自致猜疑，甚懷憂懼，謀將起兵，每宿蓍令遵世筮之，遵世云：「不須起動，自有大慶。」
units.en: Shizu, holding the capital as chief minister, feared suspicion and plotted revolt; nightly he had Zunshi divine. Zunshi said, “Do not move—great fortune will come unbidden.”
units.literal: When Emperor Shizu as chief minister kept watch in the capital, he brought suspicion on himself and was deeply fearful, planning to raise troops; each night he kept milfoil and had Zunshi divine. Zunshi said, “There is no need to move; great good fortune will come of itself.”

units.zh: 俄而趙郡王奉太後令以遺詔追世祖。
units.en: Soon the Prince of Zhao, by the empress dowager’s testament, recalled Shizu.
units.literal: Before long the Prince of Zhao Commandery, acting on the empress dowager’s order and the testamentary edict, summoned Shizu back.

units.zh: 及卽祚，授其中書舍人，固辭疾。
units.en: On his accession he offered Zunshi a secretariat post; Zunshi pleaded illness and refused.
units.literal: When he took the throne, he offered Zunshi the post of Palace Secretariat Draftsman, but Zunshi firmly pleaded illness.

units.zh: 趙輔和，清都人。
units.en: Zhao Fuhe was from Qingdu.
units.literal: Zhao Fuhe was a native of Qingdu.

units.zh: 少以明《易》善筮為館客。
units.en: From youth he mastered the Changes and milfoil and served as a house diviner.
units.literal: In youth, because he understood the Changes and was skilled at milfoil divination, he became a house guest.

units.zh: 高祖崩於晉陽，葬有日矣，世宗書令顯祖親卜宅兆相於鄴西北漳水北原。
units.en: After Gaozu died at Jinyang, Shizong ordered Xianzu to choose a tomb on the Zhang’s north bank west of Ye.
units.literal: Gaozu died at Jinyang; the burial day was set, and Shizong wrote ordering Xianzu personally to divine a tomb site and geomantic aspect on the north bank of the Zhang west of Ye.

units.zh: 顯祖與吳遵世擇地，頻卜不吉，又至一所，命遵世筮之，遇《革》，遵世等數十人咸云不可用。
units.en: Xianzu and Wu Zunshi cast repeatedly with ill results; at one site Zunshi drew Ge, and dozens agreed it was unlucky.
units.literal: Xianzu and Wu Zunshi chose ground; repeated divinations were unlucky. At another place he ordered Zunshi to divine and obtained Ge; Zunshi and several dozen others all said it could not be used.

units.zh: 輔和少年，在衆人之後，進云：「《革卦》於天下人皆凶，唯王家用之大吉。
units.en: Young Fuhe spoke last: “Ge bodes ill for commoners, but for a royal house it is excellent.
units.literal: Fuhe was young and stood behind the crowd; he advanced and said, “The hexagram Ge is ill-omened for all under Heaven, but for a royal house to use it is greatly auspicious.

units.zh: 《革彖辭》云：『湯武革命，應天順人。』」
units.en: The Ge judgment says that Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and the people."
units.literal: The Judgment of Ge says that Tang and Wu changed the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people."

units.zh: 顯祖遽登車，顧云：「卽以此地為定。」
units.en: Xianzu mounted at once and said, “This is the place.”
units.literal: Xianzu immediately mounted his carriage, turned, and said, “Let this place be fixed.”

units.zh: 卽義平陵也。
units.en: That became Yiping Tomb.
units.literal: This was Yiping Tomb.

units.zh: 有一人父疾，是人詣館別托相知者筮之，遇《泰》，筮者云：「此卦甚吉，疾愈。」
units.en: When a man’s father fell ill, a friend divined Tai for him and said, "This hexagram is very auspicious; the illness will heal."
units.literal: A man’s father was ill; the man went to the lodge and had an acquaintance he entrusted elsewhere divine for him; he obtained Tai, and the diviner said, “This hexagram is very auspicious—the illness will heal.”

units.zh: 是人喜。
units.en: The man rejoiced.
units.literal: The man was pleased.

units.zh: 出後，和謂筮者云：「《泰卦》《乾》下《坤》上，然則入土矣，豈得言吉？」
units.en: Fuhe told the diviner afterward, “Tai puts Qian under Kun—he goes into the earth; how is that auspicious?”
units.literal: After he left, Fuhe said to the diviner, “In Tai, Qian is below and Kun above—thus one enters the earth; how can you call it auspicious?”

units.zh: 果以凶問至。
units.en: Soon came word of death.
units.literal: Sure enough news of death arrived.

units.zh: 和大寧、武平中筮後宮誕男女及時日多中，遂授通直常侍。
units.en: In Daning and Wuping he divined palace births and dates with great success and was made regular attendant in direct communication.
units.literal: In the Daning and Wuping eras Fuhe divined for the inner palace on the birth of sons and daughters and the times, and mostly hit true; he was therefore appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Communication.

units.zh: 皇甫玉，不知何許人。
units.en: Huangfu Yu’s origins were unknown.
units.literal: Huangfu Yu—no one knew from what place he came.

units.zh: 善相人，常遊王侯家。
units.en: A physiognomer, he frequented the houses of nobles.
units.literal: He was skilled at physiognomy and often wandered among princes and marquises.

units.zh: 世宗自潁川振旅而還，顯祖從後，玉於道旁縱觀，謂人曰：「大將軍不作物，會是道北垂鼻涕者。」
units.en: As Shizong marched back from Yingchuan with Xianzu behind, Yu watched from the roadside: “The Grand General will not prevail—the man north of the road who wipes his nose will.”
units.literal: When Shizong returned from Yingchuan with his army in array, Xianzu followed behind; Yu watched freely by the roadside and said to someone, “The Grand General will not accomplish the enterprise; it will be the one north of the road who wipes his nose.”

units.zh: 顯祖旣卽位，試玉相術，故以帛巾袜其眼，而使歷摸諸人。
units.en: Xianzu blindfolded him and had him feel his way among the courtiers to test his art.
units.literal: After Xianzu took the throne he tested Yu’s art, therefore bound his eyes with a cloth kerchief and had him feel his way among the men.

units.zh: 至於顯祖，曰：「此是最大達官。」
units.en: At Xianzu he said, “Here is the greatest man in office.”
units.literal: Coming to Xianzu, he said, “This is the greatest eminent official.”

units.zh: 於任城王，曰：「當至丞相。」
units.en: Of Rencheng he said, “He will reach the chancellorship.”
units.literal: Of the Prince of Rencheng he said, “He will reach the chancellorship.”

units.zh: 於常山、長廣二王，並亦貴，而各私掐之。
units.en: Changshan and Changuang he also called noble—and pinched each in secret.
units.literal: Of the princes of Changshan and Changuang he also said they would be noble, and privately pinched each of them.

units.zh: 至石動統，曰：「此弄癡人。」
units.en: At Shi Dongtong he said, “A court fool.”
units.literal: Coming to Shi Dongtong, he said, “This is a playing fool.”

units.zh: 至供膳，曰：「正得好飲食而已。」
units.en: At the pantry steward: “Good meals, nothing more.”
units.literal: Coming to the food server, he said, “He will only get good food and drink.”

units.zh: 玉嘗為高歸彥相，曰：「位極人臣，但莫反。」
units.en: Reading Gao Guiyan’s face, Yu said, “You will rise to the summit of rank—only do not rebel.”
units.literal: Yu once read the physiognomy of Gao Guiyan and said, “You will reach the extreme of human rank, only do not rebel.”

units.zh: 歸彥曰：「我何為反？」
units.en: Guiyan asked, “Why would I rebel?”
units.literal: Guiyan said, “Why would I rebel?”

units.zh: 玉曰：「不然，公有反骨。」
units.en: Yu said, “You bear a rebel’s bone.”
units.literal: Yu said, “Not so—you have a rebel’s bone.”

units.zh: 玉謂其妻曰：「殿上者不過二年。」
units.en: Yu told his wife, “The throne will not hold two years.”
units.literal: Yu told his wife, “The one on the throne will not last two years.”

units.zh: 妻以告舍人斛斯慶，慶以啟帝，帝怒召之。
units.en: His wife told Husiqing, who told the emperor; the emperor summoned him in anger.
units.literal: His wife told the palace attendant Husiqing; Husiqing reported to the emperor, and the emperor angrily summoned him.

units.zh: 玉每照鏡，自言當兵死，及被召，謂其妻曰：「我今去不迴，若得過日午時，或當得活。」
units.en: Yu had long said he would die by the blade; summoned, he told his wife, “I will not return—unless I pass noon.”
units.literal: Yu whenever he looked in the mirror said he was fated to die by weapons; when summoned he told his wife, “I go now and will not return; if I can pass the noon hour, I may yet live.”

units.zh: 旣至正中，遂斬之。
units.en: At noon he was beheaded.
units.literal: When the hour reached the center he was beheaded.

units.zh: 世宗時有吳士，雙盲而妙於聲相，世宗歷試之。
units.en: In Shizong’s day a blind Wu man judged men by voice; Shizong tested him often.
units.literal: In Shizong’s time there was a man of Wu, blind in both eyes yet marvelous in voice physiognomy; Shizong tested him repeatedly.

units.zh: 聞劉桃枝之聲，曰：「有所繫屬，然當大富貴，王侯將相多死其手，譬如鷹犬為人所使。」
units.en: Hearing Liu Taozhi’s voice, he said, "He is bound to another, yet he will become very rich and noble, and many lords will die by his hand, like hawks trained for others."
units.literal: Hearing the voice of Liu Taozhi, he said, “He has something he is tied to, yet he will be very rich and noble; many kings, marquises, and chancellors will die by his hand, like hawks and dogs used by men.”

units.zh: 聞趙道德之聲，曰：「亦繫屬人，富貴翕赫，不及前人。」
units.en: Hearing Zhao Daode’s voice, he said, "He too is bound to another; he will shine with wealth and rank, but less than the former man."
units.literal: Hearing the voice of Zhao Daode, he said, “He too is tied to others; his wealth and glory blaze, but not equal to the former.”

units.zh: 聞太原公之聲，曰：「當為人主，」聞世宗之聲，不動，崔暹私掐之，乃謬言：「亦國主也。」
units.en: Taiyuan’s voice meant a throne; at Shizong’s he was silent until Cui Xian pinched him, then he lied, “A ruler too.”
units.literal: Hearing the voice of the Duke of Taiyuan, he said, “He will become a ruler.” Hearing Shizong’s voice he did not stir; Cui Xian privately pinched him, and he then falsely said, “He too is a ruler of a state.”

units.zh: 世宗以為我群奴猶當極貴，況吾身也。
units.en: Shizong thought, “If my slaves rise so high, what of me?”
units.literal: Shizong thought, “If even my slaves will reach the utmost nobility, how much more my own person.”

units.zh: 解法選，河內人。
units.en: Xie Faxuan was from Henei.
units.literal: Xie Faxuan was a native of Henei.

units.zh: 少明相術，鑒照人物，皆如其言。
units.en: From youth his mirror-reading of faces never failed.
units.literal: In youth he understood physiognomy; examining persons in a mirror, all was as he said.

units.zh: 頻為和士開相中，士開牒為府參軍。
units.en: He Shikai kept him as mansion staff after repeated favorable readings.
units.literal: He repeatedly read He Shikai’s physiognomy favorably; Shikai had him registered as a staff officer in the princely mansion.

units.zh: 魏寧，鉅鹿人。
units.en: Wei Ning was from Julu.
units.literal: Wei Ning was a native of Julu.

units.zh: 以善推祿命征為館客。
units.en: Summoned as house guest for his skill in fate calculation.
units.literal: Because he was skilled at calculating allotted fate he was summoned as a house guest.

units.zh: 武成親試之，皆中。
units.en: Wucheng tested him personally; he never missed.
units.literal: Wucheng personally tested him, and all hit true.

units.zh: 乃以己生年月託為異人而問之，寧曰：「極富貴，今年入墓。」
units.en: Wucheng disguised his birth date; Ning said, “Supreme fortune—and the tomb this year.”
units.literal: He then gave his own birth year and month, pretending to be another person and asking; Ning said, “Extremely rich and noble—this year he enters the tomb.”

units.zh: 武成驚曰：「是我！」
units.en: Wucheng cried, “That is me!”
units.literal: Wucheng said in alarm, “That is me!”

units.zh: 寧變辭曰：「若帝王，自有法。」
units.en: Ning backtracked: “Emperors follow other rules.”
units.literal: Ning changed his words and said, “If an emperor and king, he has his own method.”

units.zh: 又有陽子術，語人曰：「謠言：『盧十六，雉十四，犍子拍頭三十二。』
units.en: Master Yang cited a rhyme: “Lu sixteen, pheasant fourteen, the colt strikes his head at thirty-two.
units.literal: There was also Master Yang’s technique; he told people, “A rhyme says: ‘Lu at sixteen, pheasant at fourteen, the colt beats his head at thirty-two.’

units.zh: 且四八天之大數，太上之祚，恐不過此。」
units.en: Four eights are heaven’s great number—the Grand Supreme’s reign will not pass it.”
units.literal: Moreover four times eight is Heaven’s great number; the Grand Supreme’s reign, I fear, will not pass this.”

units.zh: 旣而武成崩，年三十二也。
units.en: Wucheng died at thirty-two, as he said.
units.literal: Before long Wucheng died, aged thirty-two.

units.zh: 綦母懷文，不知何郡人。
units.en: Qimu Huaiwen’s home commandery was unknown.
units.literal: Qimu Huaiwen—no one knew from what commandery he came.

units.zh: 以道術事高祖。
units.en: He served Gaozu with Daoist arts.
units.literal: By Daoist arts he served Gaozu.

units.zh: 武定初，官軍與周文戰於邙山。
units.en: Early in Wuding the royal army fought Zhou Wen at Mount Mang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, the government army fought Zhou Wen at Mount Mang.

units.zh: 是時官軍旗幟盡赤，西軍盡黑，懷文言於高祖曰：「赤火色，黑水色，水能滅火，不宜以赤對黑。
units.en: At this time the official army's banners were all red, and the western army's were all black. Huaiwen said to Gao Huan, "Red is the color of fire; black is the color of water. Water can extinguish fire. It is not fitting to set red against black.
units.literal: At this time the official army's banners were all red, and the western army's were all black. Huaiwen said to Gao Huan, "Red is the color of fire; black is the color of water. Water can extinguish fire. It is not fitting to set red against black.

units.zh: 土勝水，宜改為黃。」
units.en: Earth conquers water—use yellow.”
units.literal: Earth overcomes water; you should change to yellow.”

units.zh: 高祖遂改為赭黃，所謂河陽幡者。
units.en: Gaozu switched to ochre yellow—the Heyang banners.
units.literal: Gaozu therefore changed to ochre yellow—the so-called Heyang banners.

units.zh: 又造宿鐵刀，其法燒生鐵精以重柔鋌，數宿則成剛，以柔鐵為刀脊，浴以五牲之溺，淬以五牲之脂，斬甲過三十札。
units.en: He forged night-quenched blades: layer soft iron on hardened steel, quench in the five beasts’ urine and fat—the edge cut thirty layers of armor.
units.literal: He also made night-quenched iron blades: the method is to burn raw iron essence and layer soft ingots; after several nights they become hard; soft iron forms the spine of the blade; it is bathed in the urine of the five sacrificial beasts and quenched in their fat; it can cut through more than thirty layers of armor.

units.zh: 今襄國冶家所鑄宿柔鋌，乃其遺法，作刀猶甚快利，不能截三十札也。
units.en: Xiangguo smiths still use his night-soft ingots; their blades are keen but not thirty-fold.
units.literal: The night-soft ingots that smiths of Xiangguo cast today are his surviving method; blades made from them are still very sharp but cannot cut thirty layers.

units.zh: 懷文云：「廣平郡南斡子城是干將鑄劍處，其土可以瑩刀。」
units.en: Huaiwen said, "The soil at Ganzi Castle south of Guangping, where Gan Jiang forged swords, can polish blades."
units.literal: Huaiwen said, “South of Guangping Commandery, Ganzi Castle is where Gan Jiang cast swords; its earth can polish blades.”

units.zh: 懷文官至信州刺史。
units.en: Huaiwen became inspector of Xin Province.
units.literal: Huaiwen rose to Inspector of Xin Province.

units.zh: 又有孫正言，謂人曰：「我昔武定中為廣州士曹，聞城人曹普演言：『高王諸兒，阿保當為天子，至高德之承之，當滅。』」
units.en: Sun Zhengyan told people, "During Wuding, when I was a clerical officer in Guangzhou, I heard the townsman Cao Puyan say that among Gao's sons, Abao would reign, and when Degao's Chengzhi came, the line would end."
units.literal: There was also Sun Zhengyan, who told people, "In Wuding I was a clerical officer in Guang Province and heard the townsman Cao Puyan say that among Prince Gao's sons, Abao would become Son of Heaven, and when it reached Degao's Chengzhi, there would be destruction."

units.zh: 阿保謂天保，德之謂德昌也，滅年號承光，卽承之也。
units.en: Abao is Tianbao, Degao is Dechang; the doomed era Chengguang is Chengzhi.
units.literal: Abao means Tianbao, Degao means Dechang; the destroyed reign title Chengguang is precisely Chengzhi.

units.zh: 張子信，河內人也。
units.en: Zhang Zixin was from Henei.
units.literal: Zhang Zixin was a native of Henei.

units.zh: 性清凈，頗涉文學。
units.en: Quiet and literate by nature.
units.literal: By nature pure and quiet, he was fairly versed in letters.

units.zh: 少以醫術知名，恒隱於白鹿山。
units.en: Famed young as a physician, he lived as a hermit on White Deer Mountain.
units.literal: In youth he was famed for medical skill and constantly hid on White Deer Mountain.

units.zh: 時遊京邑，甚為魏收、崔季舒等所禮，有贈答子信詩數篇。
units.en: In the capital Wei Shou and Cui Jishu honored him; poems between them survive.
units.literal: He sometimes traveled to the capital and was greatly honored by Wei Shou, Cui Jishu, and others; there are several poems exchanged with Zixin.

units.zh: 後魏以太中大夫徵之，聽其時還山，不常在鄴。
units.en: Wei made him grand master of palace leisure, letting him return to the hills; he was seldom at Ye.
units.literal: Later Wei appointed him Grand Master of Palace Leisure and allowed him to return to the mountains at times; he was not constantly at Ye.

units.zh: 又善易卜風角。
units.en: He also read the Changes and the winds.
units.literal: He was also skilled in Changes divination and wind angles.

units.zh: 武衛奚永洛與子信對坐，有鵲鳴於庭樹，鬥而墮焉。
units.en: Xi Yongluo sat with Zixin when magpies fought in the courtyard tree and fell.
units.literal: Guard of Martial Valor Xi Yongluo sat facing Zixin; a magpie cried in the courtyard tree, fought, and fell.

units.zh: 子信曰：「鵲言不善，向夕若有風從西南來，歷此樹，拂堂角，則有口舌事。
units.en: Zixin said, “The magpie foretells trouble; if southwest wind brushes this tree and the hall corner at dusk, quarrels follow.
units.literal: Zixin said, “The magpie’s speech is unlucky; toward evening if wind comes from the southwest, passes this tree, and brushes the hall corner, there will be a matter of quarrel.

units.zh: 今夜有人喚，必不得往，雖敕，亦以病辭。」
units.en: If summoned tonight, refuse—even an edict; plead illness.”
units.literal: Tonight if someone summons you, you must not go; even if it is an edict, plead illness.”

units.zh: 子信去後，果有風如其言。
units.en: Wind came as he foretold.
units.literal: After Zixin left, wind came indeed as he said.

units.zh: 是夜，琅邪王五使切召永洛，且雲敕喚。
units.en: That night five envoys from the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo, claiming an edict.
units.literal: That night five envoys of the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo, saying it was an edict summons.

units.zh: 永洛欲起，其妻苦留之，稱墜馬腰折。
units.en: His wife held him back, claiming a fall had broken his waist.
units.literal: Yongluo was about to rise; his wife forcibly detained him, saying he had fallen from a horse and broken his waist.

units.zh: 詰朝而難作。
units.en: At dawn the coup erupted.
units.literal: At dawn the calamity broke out.

units.zh: 子信齊亡卒。
units.en: Zixin died with the fall of Qi.
units.literal: Zixin died when Qi perished.

units.zh: 馬嗣明，河內人。
units.en: Ma Siming was from Henei.
units.literal: Ma Siming was a native of Henei.

units.zh: 少明醫術，博綜經方，《甲乙》、《素問》、《明堂》、《本草》莫不咸誦。
units.en: He mastered medicine and the classics—Jade A, Plain Questions, Bright Hall, and the materia medica canon.
units.literal: In youth he understood medical arts and broadly mastered classical prescriptions; the Jade A, Plain Questions, Bright Hall, and Root Canon of Materia Medica—none did he not recite.

units.zh: 為人診候，一年前知其生死。
units.en: He could tell life or death a year ahead.
units.literal: When diagnosing people, he knew their life or death a year in advance.

units.zh: 邢卲子大寶患傷寒，嗣明為之診，候脉，退告楊愔云：「邢公子傷寒不治自差，然脈候不出一年便死，覺之晚，不可治。」
units.en: When Xing Shao’s son Dabao fell ill, Siming said to Yang Yin, “The cold will pass, but the pulse shows death within a year—too late to cure.”
units.literal: Xing Shao’s son Dabao had cold damage; Siming examined him and felt his pulse, then withdrew and told Yang Yin, “Young master Xing’s cold damage will heal without treatment, yet the pulse shows he will die within a year; noticed too late, it cannot be cured.”

units.zh: 楊、邢並侍宴內殿，顯祖云：「子才兒，我欲乞其隨近一郡。」
units.en: At court Xianzu said, "Zicai's son: I would like to give him a nearby commandery."
units.literal: Yang and Xing both attended a banquet in the inner hall; Xianzu said, “Zicai’s son—I wish to beg a nearby commandery for him.”

units.zh: 楊以此子年少，未合剖符，讌罷，奏云：「馬嗣明稱大寶脉惡，一年內恐死，若其出郡，醫藥難求。」
units.en: Yang objected after the feast: “Siming says Dabao’s pulse is fatal within a year—a distant post leaves him without care.”
units.literal: Yang, because the son was young and not yet fit to receive a seal, after the feast memorialized, “Ma Siming says Dabao’s pulse is ill and he may die within a year; if he goes to a commandery, medicine will be hard to obtain.”

units.zh: 遂寢。
units.en: The appointment was dropped.
units.literal: The matter was therefore dropped.

units.zh: 大寶未期而卒。
units.en: Dabao died within the year.
units.literal: Dabao died before the year was out.

units.zh: 楊令患背腫，嗣明以練石塗之便差。
units.en: Siming cured Yang’s back abscess with refined stone paste.
units.literal: When Magistrate Yang had a swelling on his back, Siming smeared refined stone on it and it healed at once.

units.zh: 作練石法：以粗黃色石鵝鴨卵大，猛火燒令赤，內淳醋中，自屑，頻燒至石盡，取石屑曝乾，搗下簁。
units.en: Refined stone: heat yellow cobbles to red, quench in vinegar until they crumble, dry and sift the powder.
units.literal: The method for making refined stone: take coarse yellow stone the size of a goose or duck egg, burn it fiercely until red, place it in pure vinegar until it crumbles, burn repeatedly until the stone is gone, take the crumbs, dry them in the sun, pound and sift.

units.zh: 和醋以塗腫上，無不愈。
units.en: Mixed with vinegar and applied, no swelling failed to heal.
units.literal: Mix with vinegar and smear on the swelling—none fail to heal.

units.zh: 後遷通直散騎常侍。
units.en: He later became regular attendant in direct communication.
units.literal: Later he was transferred to Regular Attendant in Direct Communication.

units.zh: 針灸孔穴，往往與《明堂》不同。
units.en: His acupuncture points often differed from the Bright Hall canon.
units.literal: The acupoints for needling and cautery often differed from the Bright Hall.

units.zh: 從駕往晉陽，至遼陽山中，數處見牓，云有人家女病，若有能治差者，購錢十萬。
units.en: On the road to Jinyang in Liaoyang hills, placards offered a hundred thousand cash to heal a girl.
units.literal: Following the imperial progress to Jinyang, in the mountains of Liaoyang he saw placards in several places saying a family’s daughter was ill and that whoever could cure her would receive a reward of a hundred thousand cash.

units.zh: 諸名醫多尋牓至，問病狀，不敢下手。
units.en: Famous doctors came, read the case, and dared not treat.
units.literal: Many famous physicians sought out the placards and came, asked the symptoms, and dared not treat.

units.zh: 唯嗣明獨治之。
units.en: Only Siming took the case.
units.literal: Only Siming alone treated her.

units.zh: 問其病由。
units.en: He asked how the illness began.
units.literal: He asked the origin of the illness.

units.zh: 云曾以手將一麥穟，卽見一赤物長二寸，似蛇，入其手指中，因驚怖倒地，卽覺手臂疼腫，漸及半身俱腫，痛不可忍，呻吟晝夜不絕。
units.en: She had touched a wheat ear; a red serpent-like thing two inches long entered her finger. Her arm swelled to half her body in agony day and night.
units.literal: She said she had once held an ear of wheat in her hand and at once saw a red thing two inches long, like a snake, enter her finger; startled and terrified she fell to the ground, and at once felt pain and swelling in her arm, gradually reaching the whole half of her body, with pain unbearable and groaning day and night without cease.

units.zh: 嗣明為處方服湯。
units.en: Siming gave her a decoction.
units.literal: Siming prescribed a decoction for her to drink.

units.zh: 比嗣明從駕還，女平復。
units.en: When he returned from court, she was healed.
units.literal: By the time Siming returned from following the imperial progress, the girl had recovered.

units.zh: 嗣明，隋初卒。
units.en: Siming died in early Sui.
units.literal: Siming died in the early Sui.

units.zh: 令楊愔傳旨，謂國子助教許散愁曰：「先生在世何以自資？」
units.en: He had Yang Yin deliver his message to Xu Sanchou, assistant instructor at the National University: "Sir, how do you occupy yourself in this life?"
units.literal: He had Yang Yin convey the imperial message and say to National University assistant instructor Xu Sanchou, "Sir, in this life by what do you support yourself?"

units.zh: 乙巳，太師、常山王演矯詔誅尚書令楊愔、尚書右僕射燕子獻、領軍大將軍可朱渾天和、侍中宋欽道、散騎常侍鄭子默。
units.en: On the yisi day Prince Yan of Changshan, grand preceptor, forged an edict and had executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director; Kezhuhun Tianhe, commanding general of the palace guards; Song Qindao, palace attendant; and Zheng Zimo, attendant of the scattered cavalry.
units.literal: On the yisi day the grand preceptor, Prince of Changshan Yan, forged an edict and executed Yang Yin, director of the Masters of Writing; Yanzi Xian, right vice-director of the Masters of Writing; Kezhuhun Tianhe, general-in-chief commanding the guards; Song Qindao, attendant at the palace; and Zheng Zimo, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

units.zh: 及承大位，楊愔、燕子獻、宋欽道等同輔。
units.en: When he came to the throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others served jointly as his advisers.
units.literal: When he inherited the great throne, Yang Yin, Yanzi Xian, Song Qindao, and others assisted him together.

units.zh: 以常山王地親望重，內外畏服，加以文宣初崩之日，太后本欲立之，故愔等並懷猜忌。
units.en: Prince Yan of Changshan was a close kinsman with formidable prestige, feared and obeyed at court and beyond. Since the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him when Emperor Wenxuan died, Yang Yin and the others all suspected him.
units.literal: Because the Prince of Changshan was close in kinship and weighty in reputation, and those within and without feared and submitted to him, and because on the day Emperor Wenxuan first died the empress dowager had originally wanted to enthrone him, Yin and the others all harbored suspicion.

units.zh: 股肱輔弼，雖懷厥誠，旣不能贊弘道德，和睦親懿，又不能遠慮防身，深謀衛主，應斷不斷，自取其咎。
units.en: His chief ministers may have been sincere, but they could not help him enlarge the Way and virtue or keep harmony among his kin. Nor could they plan far enough to protect themselves or safeguard their lord. When decision was needed they failed to decide, and brought disaster on themselves.
units.literal: His chief ministers and assistants, although they held sincere intentions, could neither assist him in magnifying the Way and virtue and harmonizing his close kin, nor plan farsightedly to protect themselves and deeply scheme to safeguard their lord; when they should have acted decisively they did not, and brought blame upon themselves.

units.zh: 臣旣誅夷，君壽廢辱，皆任非其器之所致爾。
units.en: The ministers were exterminated, and the ruler, though still alive, was deposed and humiliated. All of it came from entrusting affairs to men unequal to the task.
units.literal: The ministers were already executed and wiped out, while the ruler, though alive, was deposed and humiliated; all this came from entrusting office to men who were not equal to the task.

units.zh: 壬寅，魏帝詔太原公洋攝理軍國，遣中使敦喻。
units.en: On renyin day the emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang administer military and state affairs and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.
units.literal: On renyin the Wei Emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Yang administer military and state affairs, and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.

units.zh: 時太原公洋在城東雙堂，入而討賊，臠割京等，皆漆其頭。
units.en: At the time Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
units.literal: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.

units.zh: 又以河間人信都芳工算術，引之在館。
units.en: He also summoned Xin Du Fang of Hejian, a master of mathematics, to his library.
units.literal: Moreover, because Xin Du Fang of Hejian was skilled in calculation and astronomy, he brought him into his household academy.

units.zh: 其撰古今樂事九章十二圖，又集器準九篇，芳別為之注，皆行於世。
units.en: His nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music through the ages, and nine chapters on instrument measures with Fang's separate commentary, all circulated.
units.literal: He compiled nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music old and new, and also gathered nine chapters on instrument standards; Fang separately annotated them, and all circulated in the world.

units.zh: 二月己亥，以太傅、常山王演爲太師、錄尚書事，以太尉、長廣王湛爲大司馬、幷省錄尚書事，以尚書左僕射、平秦王歸彥爲司空，趙郡王叡爲尚書左僕射。
units.en: In the second month, on jihai, Prince Yan of Changshan, then grand tutor, was appointed grand preceptor and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand commandant, became grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration. Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, became minister of works, and Prince Rui of Zhaojun became left vice director.
units.literal: In the second month, on jihai, the Grand Tutor, Prince Yan of Changshan, was made Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; the Grand Commandant, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province; the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, was made Minister of Works; and Prince Rui of Zhaojun was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 皇建二年秋，天文告變，歸彥慮有後害，仍白孝昭，以王當咎。
units.en: In autumn of Huangjian 2, ominous celestial signs appeared. Guiyan feared future trouble and again told Emperor Xiaozhao that the prince was the one portended by the omen.
units.literal: In autumn of the second year of Huangjian, celestial signs announced change; Guiyan feared there would be later danger, and again told Xiaozhao that the prince was the one on whom blame would fall.

units.zh: 乃遣歸彥馳驛至晉陽宮殺之。
units.en: He therefore sent Guiyan by relay post to Jinyang Palace to kill him.
units.literal: He therefore sent Guiyan by relay horse to Jinyang Palace to kill him.

units.zh: 戊申，以常山王演爲大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，以大司馬、長廣王湛爲太傅、京畿大都督，以司徒段韶爲大將軍，以前司空、平陽王淹爲太尉，以司空、平秦王歸彥爲司徒，彭城王浟爲尚書令。
units.en: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was appointed grand chief minister, commander of all armies, and recorder of the Masters of Writing. Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, became grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region. Duan Shao, minister over the masses, became great general; Prince Yan of Pingyang, formerly minister of works, became grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, became minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng became director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: On the wushen day, Prince Yan of Changshan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing; Prince Zhan of Changguang, grand marshal, was made grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao, minister over the masses, was made great general; the former minister of works, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, minister of works, was made minister over the masses; and Prince You of Pengcheng was made director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 常山王憂悵，乃白太后誅其黨，時平秦王歸彥亦預謀焉。
units.en: Prince Yan of Changshan grew anxious and asked the empress dowager to execute that faction; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was also involved in the plot.
units.literal: The Prince of Changshan became anxious and distressed, and so reported to the empress dowager that their party should be executed; at the time Prince Guiyan of Pingqin also took part in the plot.

units.zh: 使崔季舒毆之三拳，奮衣而出。
units.en: He had Cui Jishu strike him three blows with the fist, then flung his robes aside and stormed out.
units.literal: He had Cui Jishu strike him three blows with the fist, then flung his robes and went out.

units.zh: 數日前，崔季舒無故於北宮門外諸貴之前誦鮑明遠詩曰：「將軍旣下世，部曲亦罕存。」
units.en: Days before, Cui Jishu for no apparent reason recited before the nobles outside the North Palace Gate a poem of Bao Mingyuan: "The general having left this world, his followers scarcely remain."
units.literal: Days before, Cui Jishu for no apparent reason before the nobles outside the North Palace Gate recited a poem of Bao Mingyuan: "The general having left this world, his followers scarcely remain."

units.zh: 將欲受禪，與陳元康、崔季舒等屏斥左右，署擬百官。
units.en: About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.
units.literal: About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.

units.zh: 尋遣季舒入謝。
units.en: Soon he sent Jishu in to apologize.
units.literal: Soon he sent Jishu in to apologize.

units.zh: 東魏主賜季舒彩，季舒未敢即受，啟之於王，王使取一段。
units.en: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to Gao Cheng, who told him to take one bolt.
units.literal: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to the Prince, who told him to take one bolt.

units.zh: 東魏主以四百疋與之，曰：「亦一段耳。」
units.en: The Eastern Wei emperor gave him four hundred bolts and said, "That too is only one bolt."
units.literal: The Eastern Wei emperor gave him four hundred bolts and said: "That too is only one bolt."

units.zh: 散騎常侍徐之才、館客宋景業先為天文圖讖之學，又陳山提家客楊子術有所援引，並因德政勸顯祖行禪代之事。
units.en: Regular attendant Xu Zhicai and retainer Song Jingye were versed first in astronomy and apocrypha; also Chen Shanti's household retainer Yang Zishu had connections—all through Dezheng urged Gao Yang to carry out the abdication and succession.
units.literal: Regular attendant Xu Zhicai and retainer Song Jingye were versed first in astronomy and apocrypha; also Chen Shanti's household retainer Yang Zishu had connections—all through Dezheng urged Gao Yang to carry out the abdication and succession.

units.zh: 徐之才、宋景業等每言卜筮雜占陰陽緯侯，必宜五月應天順人，德政亦勸不已。
units.en: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others kept speaking of divination, mixed auguries, yin and yang, and omens in the weft-texts — that May was the time to answer Heaven and win men; Dezheng urged on without pause.
units.literal: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others constantly spoke of divination, miscellaneous auguries, yin and yang, and the weft-texts of omens — that May was surely the time to answer Heaven and accord with men; Dezheng too urged without cease.

units.zh: 崔暹，字季倫，博陵安平人，漢尚書寔之後也，世為北州著姓。
units.en: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han minister of works, and for generations a leading house of the northern provinces.
units.literal: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han Minister of Works, and for generations a prominent clan of the northern provinces.

units.zh: 太史公敘九流，述《日者》、《龜策》、《扁鵲倉公列傳》。
units.en: Grand Historian Sima Qian surveyed the Nine Schools and wrote the biographies of day-diviners, tortoise-and-yarrow specialists, and the physicians Bian Que and Lord Cang.
units.literal: Grand Historian Sima Qian arranged the Nine Schools and composed the 'Biographies of the Day Diviners,' 'Tortoise and Yarrow,' and 'Bian Que and Lord Cang.'

units.zh: 命乃在天，雖扁鵲何益！」
units.en: The mandate is in Heaven. Though Bian Que came, what benefit!"
units.literal: The mandate is in Heaven. Though Bian Que came, what benefit!"

units.zh: 及輿駕在晉陽，武成鎮鄴，望氣者云鄴城有天子氣。
units.en: When the emperor was at Jinyang and Wucheng (Gao Zhan) held Ye, geomancers declared that Ye possessed the aura of imperial destiny.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Jinyang and Wucheng was stationed at Ye, practitioners of qi-reading said Ye city had the aura of a Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 長廣王湛為大司馬、錄幷省尚書事，解京畿大都督。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang was appointed grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Bingzhou administration, and was relieved of the capital-region command.
units.literal: Prince Zhan of Changguang was made Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing in Bing Province, and was relieved as metropolitan commander of the capital region.

units.zh: 戊子，以太傅、長廣王湛為右丞相，以太尉、平陽王淹為太傅，以尚書令、彭城王浟為大司馬。
units.en: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changguang, then grand tutor, became right chancellor; Prince Yan of Pingyang, then grand commandant, became grand tutor; and Prince You of Pengcheng, director of the Masters of Writing, became grand marshal.
units.literal: On wuzi, the Grand Tutor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, was appointed Right Chancellor; the Grand Commandant, Prince Yan of Pingyang, was appointed Grand Tutor; and the Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince You of Pengcheng, was appointed Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 遣使詔追長廣王入纂大統，手書云：「宜將吾妻子置一好處，勿學前人也。」
units.en: He dispatched envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed him, writing in his own hand: "See that my wife and children are placed somewhere safe; do not do as those before you did."
units.literal: He sent envoys with an edict summoning the Prince of Changguang to succeed to the great succession, writing in his own hand: "You should place my wife and children in a good place; do not imitate those before you."

units.zh: 帝時以尊親而見猜斥，乃與長廣王期獵，謀之於野。
units.en: Because his rank and kinship made him suspect, Xiaozhao was being pushed aside. He therefore arranged a hunt with Prince Zhan of Changguang and plotted with him in the field.
units.literal: The emperor at that time, because he was an honored kinsman, was regarded with suspicion and pushed aside; he therefore arranged to hunt with the Prince of Changguang and plotted with him in the countryside.

units.zh: 乃鑿地為十道，又用術士李業興「孤虛法」，聚攻其北。
units.en: He dug ten tunnels and used Li Yexing's "solitary and void" method, massing attack on the north.
units.literal: He then dug ten tunnels and also used the adept Li Yexing's "solitary and void" method, massing attack on the north.

units.zh: 初，子野曾祖松之，宋元嘉中受詔續修何承天《宋史》，未及成而卒，子野常欲繼成先業。
units.en: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Pei Songzhi, in the Yuanjia era of Song, had received an edict to continue He Chengtian's History of Song, but died before finishing it; Ziye had long wished to complete his ancestor's work.
units.literal: Earlier, Ziye's great-grandfather Songzhi, in the Yuanjia era of Song, received an edict to continue and revise He Chengtian's History of Song, but died before completing it; Ziye had long wished to carry on and finish his ancestor's work.

units.zh: 岐伯
units.en: Qibo
units.literal: Qibo

units.zh: 文宣大漸，以常山、長廣二王位地親逼，深以後事為念。
units.en: As Emperor Wenxuan sank toward death, he worried deeply about the aftermath, for the princes of Changshan and Changgung stood too close in kinship and power.
units.literal: When Wenxuan was critically ill, because the princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and kin and pressed near, he was deeply concerned about what would follow.

units.zh: 臣與湛等為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金等惜獻皇帝基業，共執遵彥等領入宮，未敢刑戮，專輒之失，罪合萬死。」
units.en: Your servant and Zhan took the weight of state upon ourselves; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; we seized Zunyan and his fellows and brought them into the palace. We have not yet executed them; for our presumption we deserve ten thousand deaths."
units.literal: Your servant and Zhan and the rest took state affairs as weighty; Heba Ren, Hulu Jin and the rest cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; together we seized Zunyan and the rest and led them into the palace; we did not yet dare execution and punishment; the fault of arrogating authority deserves ten thousand deaths."

units.zh: 長廣旦伏家僮數十人於錄尚書後室，仍與席上勳貴數人相知。
units.en: The prince of Changgung hid dozens of household slaves in the recorder's rear chamber and confided in several honored nobles at the banquet.
units.literal: The prince of Changgung at dawn hid several tens of household slaves in the rear chamber of the recorder of the masters of writing; moreover he made understanding with several meritorious nobles at the seat.

units.zh: 由是嬖寵失職之徒，盡歸心二叔。
units.en: Hence the displaced favorites all threw their loyalty to the two princes.
units.literal: Hence those of the favorites who lost their posts all turned their hearts to the two uncles.

units.zh: 我一曰「捉酒」，二曰「捉酒，」三曰「何不捉，」爾輩即捉。
units.en: At my first call, "seize the wine"; my second, "seize the wine"; and my third, "why not seize it?" You seize them at once.
units.literal: At my first call, "seize the wine"; my second, "seize the wine"; and my third, "why not seize it?" You seize them at once.

units.zh: 常山王欲緩之，長廣王曰：「不可。」
units.en: The prince of Changshan wished to relent; the prince of Changgung said, "No."
units.literal: The prince of Changshan wished to ease matters; the prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be."

units.zh: 仍欲以常山王隨梓宮之鄴，留長廣王鎮晉陽。
units.en: They next wished the prince of Changshan to accompany the coffin to Ye and the prince of Changgung to hold Jinyang.
units.literal: They still wished the prince of Changshan to follow the coffin to Ye and leave the prince of Changgung to garrison Jinyang.

units.zh: 愔等又議不可令二王俱出，乃奏以長廣王為大司馬、幷州刺史，常山王為太師、錄尚書事。
units.en: The regents then decided the two princes must not both leave the capital and memorialized appointing the prince of Changgung grand marshal and Bingzhou inspector, and the prince of Changshan grand preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing.
units.literal: Yin and the rest again discussed that the two princes must not both be sent out; they memorialized making the prince of Changgung Grand Marshal and inspector of Bing, the prince of Changshan Grand Preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing.

units.zh: 長廣王及歸彥在朱華門外。
units.en: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan waited outside Vermilion Flower Gate.
units.literal: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside Vermilion Flower Gate.

units.zh: 長廣王以子默昔讒己作詔書，故先拔其舌，截其手。
units.en: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in an edict, first tore out his tongue and cut off his hands.
units.literal: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in drafting an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.
